newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says power price delay "extremely serious".
newsitem.headline: Chile says power price delay "extremely serious".

text.p: Chilean Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia said delays in setting new electricity prices as the result of a dispute between the government and power firms were "extremely serious" as they hurt consumers.

The government has been widely expected to cut electricity distribution prices by up to eight percent. But the process has been held up by a court order freezing the announcement of the new prices which were due to come into force Monday.
"The government considers the delay in bringing the new rates into force extremely grave, as this affects all homes and businesses throughout the country," Garcia told reporters.
The government, which had hoped to announce the new prices last week, must publish the rates today at the latest to meet the Monday deadline.
If it fails, then the previous higher prices will remain in force until the legal impasse is resolved.

Three power companies, including distributor Chilectra, won the court ruling after they complained over the way the government was calculating the new prices which will be in force for the next four years.
The court must decide by Wednesday if it upholds the complaints or whether the tariff cuts can go ahead as planned.
Garcia said he was confident that the court would rule in favor of the national energy commission and the economy minstry which were in charge of fixing the new prices.
"We hope that the appeal court recognizes the economy ministry does not suffer any legal impediment in publishing the decree... which will benefit all the consumers in the country," he said.
